The Governor performs the functions of the executive head of the state on behalf of the Union Government. • Article 154 relates to the vesting of the executive power of the state in the Governor. • Article 168 relates to the constitution of the legislatures in the states (Governor, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council). • Article 170 relates to the composition of the Legislative Assemblies (maximum 500 and minimum 60 members).

subject: Polity
question: Who has the power to appoint the Chief Minister (CM) of a state in India?
explanation: According to Article 164 of the Constitution, the Governor of a state has the authority to appoint the Chief Minister. Usually, the Governor invites the leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly. If no party gains a clear majority, the Governor may use discretionary power to appoint the leader of the largest coalition.

subject: Polity
question: Who acts as the link between the Governor and the State Council of Ministers?
explanation: In a state, the Chief Minister serves as the main link of communication between the Governor and the Council of Ministers. They keep the Governor informed about the advice, decisions, and policies of the Cabinet. • According to Article 163 of the Constitution, the Governor acts only in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers; therefore, the Chief Minister plays a central role in this communication and coordination.

subject: Polity
question: What is the tenure of a Governor in an Indian state?
explanation: Under Article 156 of the Constitution, the normal term of a Governor is fixed at 5 years, but they hold office during the pleasure of the President. • A Governor can be removed before the completion of the term, or they may resign by submitting a resignation letter to the President.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements:
explanation: The President derives the pardoning power from Article 72, whereas the Governor is granted this power under Article 161. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect. • The Governor cannot ‘pardon’ a death sentence; the power to completely pardon a death sentence rests only with the President. Thus, statement 2 is correct. Ans. (b) State Legislature (Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council)

subject: Polity
question: Which article of the Constitution provides for the State Legislative Assemblies?
explanation: Article 168 of the Indian Constitution specifies the constitution of Legislative Assemblies in the states and their provisions. This article provides the basis for the composition and constitution of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council (where applicable). • Article 172 determines the duration of state legislatures, and Article 170 relates to the composition of Legislative Assemblies in states (maximum 500 and minimum 60 members).

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following is true regarding the Anglo-Indian representation in State Assemblies?
options: The Governor still nominates one Anglo-Indian member
The provision was abolished by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment
The provision was abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amend ment
Anglo-Indian members are elected through proportional representation
explanation: According to the 104th Constitutional Amendment, the duration of reservation for SC/STs in Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies has been extended until 25 January, 2030. • In this amendment, the nomination of the Anglo-Indian community (Articles 331 and 333) was abolished.

subject: Polity
question: Which state has a bicameral legislature?
explanation: Currently, only 6 states in India have a Bicameral Legislature (both Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council). These states are: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.

subject: Polity
question: Fill in the blanks: Even after a Bill is passed by the State Legislature, the Governor may forward it to the ___ for consideration.
explanation: Under Article 200, the Governor has the authority to reserve a State Bill for the consideration of the President. • This is specifically done when the Bill is inconsistent with the Constitution, affects Centre-State relations, or seeks to limit the powers of the High Court. Ans. (c) Functioning of the State Legislature

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following Indian states does not have a Legislative Council?
explanation: The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper and permanent house of the State Legislature, whose composition is mentioned in Article 171. At present, only 6 states in India have a bicameral system (Legislative Council): Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana. Rajasthan has only a Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).

subject: Polity
question: Members of the Legislative Council of an Indian state as nearly as may be, _______ shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify.
explanation: According to the composition of the State Legislative Council (a ‘permanent house’ and ‘upper house’) under Article 171, one-third (1/3) of the total members are elected by the members of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities. • In addition to this, 1/3 are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, and 1/6 are nominated by the Governor.

subject: Polity
question: Who can dissolve the Indian State Legislative Assembly before its term ends?
explanation: Under Article 174(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution, the Governor has the power to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly before the completion of its 5-year term. • Generally, this action is taken on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, but if the government loses its majority or there is no clear majority, the Governor can also exercise his discretion. • Just as the President dissolves the Lok Sabha under Article 85 at the Centre, similarly, the Governor dissolves the Legislative Assembly in the State.

subject: Polity
question: Who among the following is the final interpreter of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: The Supreme Court of India is the final interpreter of the Indian Constitution. This means that if any doubt or dispute arises regarding the meaning of any provision of the Constitution, the interpretation given by the Supreme Court is considered final and binding. • The Supreme Court is also called the guardian of the Constitution.

subject: Polity
question: Supreme Court can transfer cases between High Courts to another. 2. Article 139A was introduced by the 42nd Amendment.
explanation: • According to Article 139A, the Supreme Court can transfer cases involving similar legal matters from High Courts to itself or to any one High Court; therefore, statement 1 is correct. • Article 139A was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) so that uniform decisions can be made in cases involving similar laws and judicial efficiency can be increased; therefore, statement 2 is also correct.

subject: Polity
question: What is the aim of the FASTER initiative launched by the Supreme Court of India?
explanation: The objective of FASTER (Fast and Secured Transmission of Electronic Records) is to promptly transmit interim orders, stay orders, and bail orders of the court to prison authorities through a secured electronic channel. Its primary goal is to eliminate administrative delays in the release of prisoners from jails.

subject: Polity
question: The Supreme Court can adjudicate disputes between States under Article 131. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: According to Article 131, the Supreme Court has exclusive original jurisdiction in federal disputes, and not the High Courts. Under this Article, the Supreme Court settles legal disputes arising between the Centre and the States, or between two or more States. Ans. (b) 10. Consider the following statements: 1. Article 131A gave High Courts exclusive power to decide on central laws’ validity.

subject: Polity
question: It was repealed by the 43rd Constitutional Amendment. Which of the above is/are correct ?
explanation: Article 131A gave the Supreme Court, and not the High Courts, special (exclusive) jurisdiction over the validity of central laws; therefore, statement 1 is incorrect. • Article 131A was repealed by the 43rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1977; hence, statement 2 is correct.

subject: Polity
question: The strength of the sanctioned judges of the Supreme Court (SC) of India, including the Chief Justice, is_______.
explanation: Under Article 124(1) of the Indian Constitution, Parliament is empowered to determine the number of judges in the Supreme Court. Through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, this strength was increased from 31 to 34 (33 judges + 1 Chief Justice) to reduce the pendency of cases and expedite justice.

subject: Polity
question: Who was appointed as India’s 50th Chief Justice in 2022?
explanation: In 2022, Justice D.Y. Chandrachud was appointed as the 50th Chief Justice of India (CJI). He assumed office on November 9, 2022, and served until November 10, 2024. • The present and 53rd Chief Justice of India is Justice Surya Kant.

subject: Polity
question: Who is in line to become the first woman Chief Justice of the Supreme Court in India?
explanation: Justice B.V. Nagarathna is set to become the first woman Chief Justice of India (CJI) in the year 2027. The first woman judge of the Supreme Court was Justice M. Fathima Beevi (1989).

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 310 is derived from British constitutional practice 2. It grants absolute power to remove civil servants without inquiry 3. Article 311 limits the scope of Article 310 Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: The provision of Article 310 is derived from the British constitutional doctrine of “pleasure.” • Article 310 does not confer absolute power; it does not grant complete authority to remove civil servants without an inquiry. • Article 311 provides safeguards to civil servants, and thus it limits the power of Article 310.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following are included under the scope of Article 21 as interpreted by the Supreme Court? 1. Right to sleep 2. Right to shelter 3. Right to reputation 4. Right to die
explanation: The Supreme Court, while providing a broad interpretation of Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty), has included the ‘Right to Sleep’ (Ramlila Maidan Case), ‘Right to Shelter’ (Olga Tellis Case), and the Right to Dignity within its ambit. • The ‘Right to Die’ is not a fundamental right under Article 21, as it is considered antithetical (contrary) to the Right to Life.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. Parliament can bar the jurisdiction of courts over inter-state water disputes. 2. Article 262 empowers the inter- State Council to adjudicate water disputes. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: Article 262(2) empowers the Parliament to exclude the jurisdiction of courts in inter-state water disputes, on the basis of which the Inter-State Water Disputes Act was enacted. • Article 262 does not provide for the Inter-State Council, but rather for the settlement of disputes through a special tribunal. The Inter-State Council comes under Article 263 and its function is advisory and coordination, not adjudication. Ans. (a) 9. Consider the following statements: 1. Article 131 provides exclusive original jurisdiction to High Courts in federal disputes.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following disputes falls under the Supreme Court’s exclusive original jurisdiction as per Article 131 of the Indian Constitution?
options: Election disputes of MPs and MLAs
Disputes between Centre and one or more States
explanation: • Article 131 grants the Supreme Court exclusive original jurisdiction, which means that legal disputes between the Centre and the States can be heard directly only in the Supreme Court. • Inter-state water disputes (Article 262) are outside the exclusive original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court. Ans. (c) 12. Consider the statements:

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following is NOT a qual ification for the appointment of Su preme Court judges?
options: Judge of a High Court for at least five years
Advocate of a High Court for at least ten years
Advocate of the Supreme Court for at least ten years
A distinguished jurist in the opin ion of the President
explanation: According to Article 124(3) of the Constitution of India, the following qualifications are required for appointment to the post of a Supreme Court Judge: • The person must be a citizen of India. • The person has been for at least five years a Judge of a High Court (or of two or more such High Courts in succession). • The person has been for at least ten years an advocate of a High Court (or of two or more such High Courts in succession). • The person is, in the opinion of the President, a distinguished jurist. Ans. (c) High Court

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following High Courts has jurisdiction over more than one state?
explanation: The Gauhati High Court is an example of a common High Court for two or more states under Article 231 of the Indian Constitution. Earlier, its jurisdiction extended over seven northeastern states, but after 2013, separate High Courts were established for Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura. • At present, it has jurisdiction over four states— Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh.

subject: Polity
question: Who has the authority to appoint a Sessions Judge of one sessions division as an Additional Sessions Judge of another division?
explanation: The High Court has the authority to appoint a Sessions Judge of one sessions division as an Additional Sessions Judge in another division. • This power comes under the administrative control of the High Court.

subject: Polity
question: As per State of the Judiciary Report 2023, women constitute of the working strength of the district judiciary.
explanation: • According to the ‘State of the Judiciary Report 2023’ released by the Centre for Research and Planning of the Supreme Court, the participation of female judicial officers in the district judiciary of India is approximately 36.3%. • According to some other reports, the participation of women in High Courts is only 13.4%.

subject: Polity
question: Which body has the power to amend the Union and State power distribution under the Indian Constitution?
explanation: In the Indian Constitution, the process of amending the distribution of powers between the Union and the States (such as the lists in the Seventh Schedule) is very important. • Under Article 368 of the Constitution, only Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution. • Since the distribution of powers is a part of the federal structure, Parliament alone cannot change it. For this, the following procedure is necessary: • A special majority in both Houses of Parliament (2/3 of the members present and voting). • Approval by a simple majority of the legislatures of at least half of the States.

subject: Polity
question: Article 263 empowers Parliament to establish Inter-State Council 2. The Council can investigate inter- state disputes 3. Its composition includes PM and Union Ministers Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: Article 263 empowers the President, rather than the Parliament, to establish the Inter-State Council. • One of the primary functions of the Inter-State Council is to investigate and discuss inter-state disputes. • The composition of the Inter-State Council includes the Prime Minister (Chairman) and Union Ministers (along with the Chief Ministers of the states).

subject: Polity
question: Criminal law is exclusively under the Union List 2. Agriculture is a State subject 3. Trade and commerce within a State falls under the State List Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: • Criminal law falls under the Concurrent List, on which both the Centre and the states can make laws. • Agriculture and trade and commerce within the state are subjects of the State List, while intra-state trade also falls under the State List. Therefore, statements 2 and 3 are correct.

subject: Polity
question: Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263. 2. Its recommendations are binding on the Union and States. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: Under Article 263 of the Constitution of India, the President has been given the power to establish an Inter-State Council; therefore, it has a constitutional basis. The Inter-State Council is an advisory body; its recommendations are not binding.

subject: Polity
question: Article 246A grants exclusive power to Parliament to make laws on GST 2. States have no legislative power over intra-state GST 3. GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: Article 246A empowers both the Parliament and the State Legislatures to make laws regarding GST; it does not grant exclusive or sole authority to the Parliament. Therefore, Statement 1 is incorrect. • The power to legislate on inter-state supply (IGST) rests exclusively with the Parliament; the States do not have this power. Therefore, Statement 2 is incorrect. • The GST Council is a constitutional body formed under Article 279A of the Indian Constitution; hence, Statement 3 is correct.

subject: Polity
question: Under which of the following circumstances the Parliament of India can legislate on the matters listed in the State List?
options: If there is a need to regulate local government elections
If there is a need to impose state- level taxes
If there is a need to appoint new state ministers
If there is a need to implement an international treaty
explanation: According to the 7th Schedule of the Indian Constitution, the power to make laws on subjects in the ‘State List’ rests solely with the State Legislatures. • However, the Indian federal system provides for certain special circumstances where the Center (Parliament) can intervene in state subjects. • Article 253 specifically empowers the Parliament to make laws on any subject in the State List to give effect to any international treaty, agreement, or convention. The consent of the states is not required for this.

subject: Polity
question: The Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction in such disputes Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: • Article 262 empowers the Parliament to make laws for the adjudication of inter-state river water disputes and to establish tribunals; therefore, statement 1 is correct. • Under Article 262(2), the Parliament may by law exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts in respect of inter-state water disputes; therefore, statement 2 is incorrect.

subject: Polity
question: In case of conflict, State law prevails over Union law Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: Both the Centre and the States can make laws on subjects mentioned in the Concurrent List; therefore, statement 1 is correct. • In case of a conflict, the law made by the Centre prevails over the law made by the State (Article 254), therefore statement 2 is incorrect. • Union List: Only the Centre makes laws. • State List: Generally, the States make laws.

subject: Polity
question: Article 246A allows States to legislate on intra-state supply of goods and services. Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: The recommendations of the GST Council are not considered binding because they are based on the cooperation between the Centre and the States. Therefore, Statement 1 is incorrect. • Under Article 246A, the State has the power to make laws regarding intra-state supply; hence, Statement 2 is correct. Note: Only the Parliament has the power to make laws regarding inter- state supply.

subject: Polity
question: Under what circumstances can the Parliament legislate on a subject in the State List?
options: When Rajya Sabha passes a resolution
explanation: Under Article 249 of the Constitution, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority of its members present and voting that a subject in the ‘State List’ is of ‘National Interest’, then Parliament can make laws on it. This provision grants the Centre authority over state subjects under special circumstances within the federal structure of India.

subject: Polity
question: What is the primary function of the Inter-State Council?
explanation: The main function of the Inter- State Council, established under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution, is to investigate and advise on disputes arising between states and to enhance coordination in Centre-State relations. • It is chaired by the Prime Minister, and the Chief Ministers of all states are its members. This council is an important platform for strengthening Cooperative Federalism.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. Inter-State Council was established in 1990 on the recommendation of Sarkaria Commission 2. It is a constitutional body under Article 263. 3. It has powers to enforce compliance among States Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 as a constitutional body under Article 263 of the Constitution, based on the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission. It is an advisory body chaired by the Prime Minister, aimed at enhancing coordination and cooperation between the Centre and the States, as well as among the States.

subject: Polity
question: Fill in the blanks: The Sarkaria Commission (Centre-State Relations) was set up in the year ___.
explanation: The Sarkaria Commission was constituted in the year 1983. This commission was formed with the objective of reviewing Centre–State relations and strengthening the federal system.

subject: Polity
question: In case of a conflict between Central and State law on a Concurrent List subject, the State law prevails only if:
options: It is passed by a two-thirds majority
It is supported by a Supreme Court ruling
explanation: Under Article 254 of the Constitution, if there is a conflict between the laws of the Centre and the State on any subject in the Concurrent List, the law of the Centre generally prevails. However, according to Article 254(2), if a State law receives the assent of the President, it is considered effective over the Central law within that specific State.

subject: Polity
question: Seventh Schedule of the Indian constitution deals with the_________.
options: Power, authority, and re sponsibilities of Panchayats
Power, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities
explanation: Article 246 of the Constitution, through the Seventh Schedule, clarifies the division of powers between the Centre and the States. It includes three lists- Union List (Centre only), State List (State only), and Concurrent List (both), which strengthen the federal structure of India.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following subjects falls under the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution?
explanation: The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution defines the division of powers between the Centre and the States. It includes three lists – Union List, State List, and Concurrent List (both the Centre and the States can make laws). • Criminal law (matters of punishment) comes under the Concurrent List. • Police is a subject of the State List, whereas radio, television, and foreign affairs come under the Union List. Ans. (b) 10. Consider the following statements:

subject: Polity
question: Which Article enables the President to establish an Inter-State Council?
explanation: Article 263 of the Indian Constitution relates to the power of the President to establish an Inter-State Council. • Article 264: Addresses financial relations between the Central Government and the States. • Article 312: Relates to the creation of All India Services. • Article 262: Relates to the adjudication of inter-state water disputes.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council (ISC) is/ are correct? 1. The Inter-State Council is headed by the Prime Minister of India 2. It functions as a recommendatory body rather than a tribunal for dispute resolution.
explanation: The constitutional basis of the Inter-State Council is Article 263; it is established by the President and chaired by the Prime Minister, while Chief Ministers of States/Union Territories and Union Ministers are its members. • It is an advisory/recommendatory body (not a tribunal), whose objective is to promote coordination between the Centre and States as well as among States, discussion on disputes, and cooperation on subjects of common interest. Ans. (c) 13. Consider the following statements:

subject: Polity
question: What is the role of Article 263 in maintaining Union–State coordination?
explanation: Article 263: It provides for the establishment of an ‘Inter-State Council’ to ensure coordination between the Centre and the States. It is a constitutional body that is not permanent; the President has the power to establish it, and it was formed for the first time in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission.

subject: Polity
question: Fill in the blanks: The Union Home Minister chairs a Zonal Council meeting as ______ chairman .
explanation: The Chairman of the Zonal Council is the Union Home Minister of India, who automatically becomes its ex-officio Chairman by virtue of his position or office. The Chief Ministers of the states in each zone act as Vice-Chairmen on a rotational basis. Ans. (a) 16. Consider the following statements: 1. Article 262 empowers Parliament to set up tribunals for river disputes

subject: Polity
question: Which Article empowers the Parliament to create laws on State List subjects under national interest?
explanation: Under Article 249, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest, the Parliament can make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List. • Such a resolution remains in force for a period of one year and can be extended further for a period of one year at a time. Ans. (a) 18. Consider the following statements: 1. The Concurrent List allows both Centre and States to legislate.

subject: Polity
question: Under Article 262 of the Indian Constitution, which of the following interpretations most accurately reflects Parliament’s authority regarding inter- State water disputes?
options: Legislate on river navigation but not bar SC jurisdiction
Set up tribunals for water disputes and bar SC review
Mandate ISC mediation before court action
explanation: Under Article 262, Parliament may by law provide for the adjudication of inter-state water disputes and can exclude the jurisdiction of the courts. • Under this power, the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 was enacted.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements is/ are correct? 1. If a State law on a Concurrent List subject is reserved for the President and receives assent, it overrides the existing Union law on the same subject in that state. 2. Parliament can later nullify such a State law by passing another law on the same subject.
explanation: According to Article 254, if a State law on a subject in the Concurrent List receives the assent of the President, it prevails over the federal law in that State. Therefore, statement 1 is correct. • Parliament can later repeal or amend that State law by making a new law on the same subject; therefore, statement 2 is also correct.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following commissions recommended the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter- State Council to institutionalize centre- state cooperation ?
explanation: Based on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission (1983), the Inter-State Council was established under Article 263 for Centre-State cooperation, and a permanent secretariat was set up for the management of its functions. • Rajamannar Committee: Focused on greater autonomy for states (Tamil Nadu). • Punchhi Commission: Recommen dations on various aspects of Cen tre-State relations; however, the ma jor recommendation for a permanent secretariat belongs to the Sarkaria Commission. • Venkatachaliah Commission: Na tional Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution. Ans. (c) Administrative Relations

subject: Polity
question: Which committee was instrumental in recommending changes to the Centre- State relations in India?
explanation: • The Sarkaria Commission (1983) was set up to review Centre-State relations in India and to make them more robust and balanced. • This Commission recommended several important reforms related to legislative, executive, and financial relations. • Its primary objective was to strengthen cooperative federalism.

subject: Polity
question: What is the maximum number of members in a State Legislative Assembly as per the Constitution?
explanation: According to Article 170 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum number of members in a State Legislative Assembly is fixed at 500, and the minimum number is fixed at 60. However, under special provisions, exemptions in the minimum number have been granted to smaller states like Sikkim (32) and Sikkim (40).

subject: Polity
question: Which committee was instrumental in recommending changes to the Centre- State relations in India?
explanation: The Sarkaria Commission (1983) was set up to review Centre-State relations in India and to make them more robust and balanced. This Commission recommended several important reforms related to legislative, executive, and financial relations. Its primary objective was to strengthen cooperative federalism.

subject: Polity
question: The Contingency Fund of an Indian State is held by__________.
explanation: Under Article 267(2), states are empowered to establish their own Contingency Fund. This fund is placed at the disposal of the Governor and is used for making advances for the purpose of meeting unforeseen expenditure (such as during a natural disaster) pending authorization by the State Legislature.

subject: Polity
question: Arrange the following in chronological order: A) Sarkaria Commission report submitted B) Inter-State Council constituted C) Punchhi Commission constituted
explanation: Sarkaria Commission (1988): A commission to review Centre-State relations, whose major recommendation was the establishment of the Inter-State Council. • Inter-State Council (1990): A permanent constitutional forum established under Article 263, which coordinates and resolves disputes between states. • Punchhi Commission (2007): The second commission on Centre-State relations, which gave suggestions on internal security and the role of the Governor. Ans. (a) 27. Consider the following statements:

subject: Polity
question: The system of federalism in India divides power between:
explanation: The system of federalism in India is based on the constitutional division of powers between the Central and State governments, which is defined through the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.

subject: Polity
question: Read the below statements related to Concurrent List laws: 1. Union law overrides state law in conflict. 2. State law can prevail if reserved and assented by President. Which is/are correct?
explanation: On subjects in the Concurrent List, both the Centre and the State can make laws. However, if there is any conflict between the two laws, then according to the general rule, the law made by Parliament (Centre) prevails. • If a State law is reserved for the consideration of the President and the President gives assent to it, then that law is considered valid in that State even if it is in conflict with the Central law. However, Parliament can later amend or repeal that law.

subject: Polity
question: Which list allows both Centre and State to legislate on the same subject?
explanation: List Power to make Major examples laws Union Only Cen Defence, Banking, Foreign Affairs, Railways List tre (Par liament) State Only State Police, Agriculture, Public Health, Jail List Legisla ture Con current Both Centre and State Education, Con servation of Wild life, Population Control List Ans. (c) Financial Relations

subject: Polity
question: In India, which of the following statements is correct about the financial relationship between the Center and the States?
options: The Union Government has exclusive control over all types of taxation, including state taxes.
The States have no role in the allocation of taxes and resources, and all funds are directly managed by the Union.
The Union Government collects taxes and distributes them between the Union and the States through the Finance Commission.
States have the authority to impose taxes on defense, currency, and foreign trade.
explanation: Under Article 280, the President of India constitutes a Finance Commission every five years. Its main function is to recommend the equitable distribution of taxes collected by the Center (like Income Tax, GST share) between the Central and State governments.

subject: Polity
question: Fill in the blanks: The Chairperson of the GST Council is the________ of India.
explanation: The Chairperson of the GST Council is the Union Finance Minister of India, and it includes the Finance Ministers of the States or any other Minister nominated by them as members. • The GST Council makes recommenda -tions to the Centre and the States on issues related to GST; its formation process is described under Article – 279A.

subject: Polity
question: There is a constitutional requirement in India to present the annual financial statement before the ____ every year.
explanation: According to Article 112 of the Indian Constitution, it is a constitutional requirement to present the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) before the Parliament every year. • In this, a statement of the government’s estimated receipts and expenditure is presented. • Although the budget is presented on behalf of the President, constitutionally it is placed before the Parliament.

subject: Polity
question: To which level of government do taxes on railway fares and freights accrue?
explanation: The tax levied on railway fares and freight is received by the Union Government because Railways is a subject included in the Union List of the Indian Constitution; therefore, the authority to levy and collect taxes related to it lies with the Central Government.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following accurately describes the legal and institutional basis of “Special Category State” status in India?
options: It is constitutional provision under Article 275
It is defined in the Constitution and recommended by Inter-State Council
It is not mentioned in the Constitution and granted by the National Development Council
It is conferred by Finance Commission under Article 280
explanation: The status of “Special Category State” is not defined in the Constitution of India. It was an administrative and policy-related concept, introduced by the National Development Council under the Gadgil formula. • Its objective was to provide additional central assistance to states with backward, hilly, border, or structural difficulties. Ans. (c) 36. Consider the following statements:

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements is/ are correct regarding the borrowing powers of States in India? 1. A State requires the Centre’s consent for internal borrowing if it owes any debt to the Centre 2. No State can raise loans from foreign sources without prior approval of the Union Government.
explanation: According to Article 293(3) of the Indian Constitution, if a State has any outstanding loan from the Central Government, that State cannot raise a new internal loan without the prior consent of the Centre. Therefore, statement 1 is true. • In accordance with India’s foreign policy and sovereignty, no State can directly take loans from foreign entities or countries; for this, the approval and guarantee of the Central Government are mandatory. Therefore, statement 2 is true.

subject: Polity
question: What does Article 268 of the Indian Constitution primarily deal with?
options: Service tax levied by Union and collected by States
Income tax levied and collected by States
Stamp duties levied by Union but collected by States
Excise duties on medicinal products collected by States
explanation: According to Article 268 of the Constitution of India, certain taxes, especially stamp duties, are levied by the Union, but their collection is done by the states and the revenue is retained by the states. • According to Article 268, certain stamp duties (such as on bills of exchange, cheques, etc.) are levied by the Union Government, but their collection and revenue accrue to the states.

subject: Polity
question: Fill in the blanks: Taxes on interstate trade are restricted by Article ____ unless Parliament otherwise provides.
explanation: Under Article 286, States cannot impose taxes even on inter-state trade without the permission of Parliament, and State governments cannot impose taxes on supplies taking place outside the State or during import-export. • Its objective is to maintain the freedom of trade and prevent double taxation.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements correctly applies the weighted voting mechanism under Article 279A(9) of the Indian Constitution?
options: The Centre holds 75% of the voting power in the GST Council
A GST Council decision can be passed solely with the support of the Centre and one State
The States collectively have twice the voting weight of the Centre in the GST council.
Each State has equal weightage as the Centre in GST council voting.
explanation: Article 279A(9) provides the procedure for decision-making in the Goods and Services Tax Council. There are 3 main points regarding its voting structure:– • 1. Weightage of Central Government: One-third (1/3) of the total votes cast. • 2. Weightage of State Governments: Two-thirds (2/3) of the total votes cast by all states combined. • 3. Mandatory Quorum: The presence of one-half (50%) of the total members is necessary for a meeting of the Council. Ans. (c) 41. Consider the following statements: 1. The GST Council makes binding recommendations on GST rates.

subject: Polity
question: Article 246A gives powers to both Parliament and States to make laws on:
explanation: The 101st Amendment, through Article 246A, provides the Centre and States the concurrent power to make laws on GST. • In this, the control of inter-state trade (IGST) has been kept exclusively with the Parliament. • The Right to Property is related to Article 300A.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements regarding Article 270 are correct? 1) Article 270 governs the sharing of taxes between the Union and States, including proceeds from GST. 2) After the 101st Constitutional Amendment, Article 270 includes provisions for distributing revenue from Union taxes and GST. 3) The GST Compensation Cess is also shared between the Union and States under Article 270.
explanation: The main function of Article 270 is to distribute the taxes collected by the Union (Centre), (including GST), between the Centre and the States. • Following the 101st Constitution Amendment (2016), the revenue received from GST was included in the divisible pool under Article 270, which is distributed between the Centre and the States by the President on the recommendation of the Finance Commission.

subject: Polity
question: Under which article can the President declare a National Emergency?
explanation: Article 352 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to declare a National Emergency in the event of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. • In this situation, the powers of the Central Government increase and the autonomy of the states becomes limited, so that the security and unity of the country are maintained.

subject: Polity
question: Under Article 352, what legislative consequence follows a Proclamation of National Emergency in India?
options: States retain exclusive control over the State List
Parliament can legislate on any matter in the State List
Rajya Sabha’s approval is required for all State Bills
President dissolves all State Legislative Assemblies
explanation: During a National Emergency under Article 352, the extensive legislative powers of the Central Government are significantly expanded. • During this period, the Parliament acquires the power to make laws on subjects mentioned in the State List. • Such laws cease to have effect six months after the Emergency has ceased to operate (unless they are extended by the Parliament).

subject: Polity
question: Which Article allows Parliament to legislate on a subject in the State List during a National Emergency?
explanation: Article 250: This empowers the Parliament to legislate on subjects mentioned in the State List during a National Emergency (Article 352). However, such laws become ineffective 6 months after the emergency has ceased to operate. • Article 256: It empowers the Central Government to give directions to the States to ensure compliance with the laws made by the Union.

subject: Polity
question: A Proclamation of National Emergency must be approved by each House within how many months?
explanation: The proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution must be approved by each House of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) within 1 month (30 days). • Once approved, the Emergency continues for 6 months. It can be extended for an indefinite period by obtaining fresh approval every 6 months. Ans. (a) State Emergency/President’s Rule/ Constitutional Emergency

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements is true in relation to the enforcement of President’s Rule?
options: The Governor’s recommendation can lead to dismissal of a State government, even if it enjoys a majority
It can be extended indefinitely with the consent of the Prime Minister
The President cannot impose President’s Rule unless the Supreme Court permits.
President’s Rule can be declared without Parliament’s approval
explanation: According to Article 356, if the Governor feels that there is a failure of constitutional machinery in the state, he can send a recommendation to the President regarding the imposition of President’s Rule. Even if the government has a majority, if ‘constitutional failure’ is found, President’s Rule can be imposed and the government can be dismissed.

subject: Polity
question: How does Article 356 impact the federal structure of india?
options: It allows Centre to dismiss State governments
explanation: Under Article 356, if the constitutional machinery fails in any state, the President can impose President’s Rule there, by which the state government can be dissolved and the governance comes under the Centre. • Due to this provision, the Central Government gets more control over the states, which weakens the federal balance and affects the autonomy of the states.

subject: Polity
question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is President’s Rule in a State proclaimed?
explanation: President’s Rule is imposed in a state under Article 356 of the Indian Constitution. • In this situation, the state government is either dismissed or suspended, and the administration of the state comes directly under the control of the central government. • Article 371 relates to special provisions for some states.

subject: Polity
question: What does Article 356 empower the President to do, and what are its constitutional safeguards?
options: Dissolve Parliament; no further approval required
Dismiss State government; needs approval within two months
Declare Financial Emergency; approval by Rajya Sabha
Suspend Fundamental Rights; needs Supreme Court approval
explanation: If it is not possible to govern a state in accordance with the Constitution, the President can impose President’s rule, due to which the State Council of Ministers is dismissed/suspended and the administration comes under the control of the Centre. • It is mandatory for the proclamation of President’s rule to be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months; if it is not approved, it automatically ceases to operate, and any extension of it is also possible only with the approval of Parliament.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements is/ are correct regarding the role of the Rajya Sabha in special legislative and emergency situations? 1. Under Article 249, a Rajya Sabha resolution allowing Parliament to legislate on State List subjects remains valid for one year 2. The Parliament can extend a proclamation of President’s Rule only with the concurrence of the Rajya Sabha
explanation: According to Article 249, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a 2/3 majority that it is necessary in the national interest for Parliament to make laws on a subject in the State List, then that resolution remains effective for one year (and it can be extended for one year at a time). • The approval of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha is necessary for the proclamation/extension of President’s Rule (Article 356), not just that of the Rajya Sabha.

subject: Polity
question: Under which constitutional provision can the President of India assume legislative powers for a state?
options: When Article 356 is invoked due to constitutional breakdown in the state
When the Lok Sabha is dissolved
On recommendation of the Prime Minister
When directed by the Supreme Court
explanation: Under Article 356 (President’s Rule), when the constitutional machinery fails in a state, the President can take the legislative powers of that state into his own hands. • In this situation, the Parliament performs the functions of the state legislature and the President empowers the Parliament to make laws for the state.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements is/ are correct? 1. The Governor’s discretionary power to recommend President’s Rule is mentioned in Article 356(1) 2. The 41st Constitutional Amend ment curtailed the Governor’s term from 5 years to 4 years 3. The Sarkaria Commission advised that Governors should not be re moved before completing their term unless in rare and compel ling circumstances
explanation: Under Article 356(1), the Governor can send a report to the President to provide information regarding the failure of constitutional machinery in the state; hence, Statement 1 is correct. • Under the 41st Constitutional Amendment (1976), the retirement age of the chairpersons and members of the PSC was increased from 60 to 62 years. Therefore, Statement 2 is incorrect. • The Sarkaria Commission (1983) recommended that Governors should not be removed arbitrarily so that the dignity and stability of the post are maintained; hence, Statement 3 is correct. Ans. (b) Financial emergency

subject: Polity
question: Which Article provides the President with the power to declare Financial Emergency?
explanation: Article 360 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency. • Article 365 relates to action against a State on failure to comply with the directions given by the Union, as it considers the non-compliance with the Union’s directions as a ‘failure of the constitutional machinery’.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following accurately reflects the constitutional provisions and historical application of Financial Emergency under Article 360?
options: No Financial Emergency has ever been declared, but it allows salary cuts of SC judges
A Financial Emergency was declared during the 1991 economic crisis
Article 360 allows states to withhold salaries of central employees
During a Financial Emergency, only the President can dismiss the Union Cabinet
explanation: Under the constitutional provisions for financial emergency, a financial emergency has never been declared in India; its declaration allows for the reduction of salaries of all central and state employees, including the judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

subject: Polity
question: Fill in the blanks: During a Financial Emergency, the salaries of judges can be reduced by the ___.
explanation: Under a Financial Emergency, the President is empowered to reduce the salaries of Central and State government employees, including the judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts. • There are three types of emergencies in India: National Emergency (Article 352), State Emergency/President’s Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360), during which the powers of the Centre increase in extraordinary circumstances.

subject: Polity
question: A majority of the total membership of the House and a majority of not less than _______ of the members present and voting is required for adoption of effective clauses and motions for consideration and passing of Constitution Amendment Bills.
explanation: Under Article 368 of the Constitution, a ‘special majority’ is required to amend the Constitution. A majority of at least two- thirds (2/3) of the members present and voting in the House is mandatory.

subject: Polity
question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor?
explanation: Under Part XX of the Constitution, Article 368 grants the Parliament the power to amend any part of the Constitution (except the basic structure). • This procedure has been taken from the Constitution of South Africa. Amending the Constitution requires a simple majority, a special majority, and in some cases, ratification by the States. Ans. (b) Important constitutional amendments

subject: Polity
question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made the Right to Education a Fundamental Right in India?
explanation: Through the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, a new Article 21A was added to the Constitution, which makes free and compulsory education for all children aged 6 to 14 years a Fundamental Right. • The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 mainly relates to co-opera tive societies. • The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, also called the Mini Con stitution, added the words Socialist, Secular, and Integrity in the Pream ble, and for the first time included 10 Fundamental Duties. • The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right.

subject: Polity
question: Which Constitutional Amendment made it mandatory for States to establish Panchayati Raj Institutions as units of local self-governance?
explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 of the Constitution of India makes it mandatory for states to establish Panchayati Raj institutions as units of local self- government. • Under this, Part IX (Articles 243- 243O) was added, and the three- tier Panchayati Raj system (Gram, Panchayat Samiti/Block, Zila Parishad) was granted constitutional status.

subject: Polity
question: Which constitutional amendment is known as the “Mini Constitution”?
explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 is called the “Mini Constitution” because it made comprehensive changes to the Constitution. • Through this, the words “Socialist”, “Secular” and “Integrity” were added to the Preamble and the tenure of the Lok Sabha was increased. This amendment strengthened the powers of the Centre and emphasized the supremacy of Parliament. • Additionally, 5 subjects such as education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List.

subject: Polity
question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) aimed at legal reform in which of the following areas?
explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 aimed to provide constitutional status to and empower local self-government (Panchayati Raj System) at the rural level. It made provisions for the structure, powers, tenure, and reservation of Panchayats.

subject: Polity
question: Education is now placed under which list after the 42nd Amendment?
explanation: Through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, five subjects, including education (forests, protection of wild animals and birds, weights and measures, administration of justice), were moved from the State List to the Concurrent List. • Presently, the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution comprises the Union List (100 subjects), the State List (61 subjects), and the Concurrent List (52 subjects).

subject: Polity
question: The Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2025 aims to: I. Abolish Waqf board completely II. Streamline the management of Waqf properties
explanation: The primary objective of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 is not to abolish the Waqf Boards, but to streamline the management of Waqf properties, bring transparency, and ensure accountability. This Act, which amends the Waqf Act, 1995, was introduced on August 8, 2024.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution made Sikkim a full-fledged State of the India?
explanation: Through the 36th Constitutional Amendment (1975), Sikkim was granted the status of a full-fledged state as the 22nd state of the Indian Union. Prior to this, Sikkim was given the status of an ‘Associate State’ by the 35th Amendment (1974).

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution replaced the term “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion” in the context of a national emergency?
explanation: To prevent the misuse of Emergency (1975), the Janata Party government passed the 44th Constitutional Amendment in 1978. Through this, for the declaration of National Emergency under Article 352, the vague term ‘internal disturbance’ was replaced by the term ‘armed rebellion’.

subject: Polity
question: By which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
explanation: By the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1989, the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by amending Article 326 of the Constitution. The objective of this amendment was to make the youth active participants in the democratic and political process of the country by the then Rajiv Gandhi government.

subject: Polity
question: G.S.T. was implemented through which constitutional amendment act of constitution of India?
explanation: In India, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) was given constitutional status through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 and was implemented across the country from 1 July 2017. • The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015 is related to the India- Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement. • Constitutional status was granted to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) by the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018. • Under the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, a provision was made for 10% reservation for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)

subject: Polity
question: What is the maximum number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, allowed in the Council of Ministers as per the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 of constitution of India?
options: 10% of the total strength of Parliament
12% of the total strength of the House of the People
15% of the total strength of the House of the People
explanation: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act (2003) restricted the uncontrolled expansion of the Council of Ministers in Indian democracy. This amendment specifically makes changes in Article 75 (for the Centre) and Article 164 (for the States). • According to Article 75(1A), the number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha. Its objective is to prevent unnecessary ministerial positions

subject: Polity
question: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 of the Indian Constitution is related with which of the following?
options: Limiting the size of the Council of Ministers
No enhancement of seats of Lok sabha and vidhan sabha til 2026
Bifurcation of the National commission of SC and ST
Fixed the strength of the Goa Legislative Assembly at a minimum of 30 members
explanation: The objective of the 91st Amendment Act, 2003 of the Indian Constitution is to prevent the unnecessary expansion of the Council of Ministers by limiting its size and to make governance more efficient and disciplined. • According to this amendment, changes were made in Article 75 and Article 164 of the Constitution, and it was stipulated that the number of members of the Council of Ministers in the Center and States cannot be more than 15% of the total number of members of the respective House.

subject: Polity
question: Which constitutional amendment granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
explanation: • The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 of the Constitution of India grants constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. • Under this amendment, Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) was added, the three-tier Panchayati Raj system was made mandatory, and provisions such as regular elections, reservation, and the Finance Commission were ensured. • The 52nd Constitutional Amendment (1985) is related to the Anti-Defection Law.

subject: Polity
question: By which Constitutional Amendment was education transferred to the Concurrent List?
explanation: • By the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, five subjects including education were moved from the State List to the Concurrent List. • By the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, the voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years.

subject: Polity
question: Through which Constitutional Amendment was Article 21A introduced, mandating free and compulsory education for children between 6 and 14 years?
explanation: • Article 21A was added to the Constitution through the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. • Changes were made to Article 45 (Directive Principles of State Policy) and the 11th Fundamental Duty (Article 51A(k)) for parents was added.

subject: Polity
question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is often referred to as the “Mini- Constitution” due to the extensive changes it introduced to the Indian Constitution?
explanation: • The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) introduced comprehensive changes to the Constitution, which is why it is called the “Mini-Constitution.” • Through this amendment, extensive changes were made to the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy, Judiciary, Executive, and Centre-State relations. • 44th Amendment: Reforms in emergency provisions; the Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights and made a legal right. • 52nd Amendment: Related to the Anti-Defection Law. • 86th Amendment: Related to the Right to Education.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister?
explanation: • Before the 42nd Amendment, Article 74(1) stated that “The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister shall aid and advise the President in the discharge of his duties”. • The 42nd Amendment (1976) made the advice binding. However, the 44th Amendment (1978) added that the President may first send back the advice for reconsideration. But if the Council of Ministers sends the same advice to the President again, he has to accept it.

subject: Polity
question: The minimum age to vote in Indian State Legislative Election is______.
explanation: According to Article 326 of the Indian Constitution, the minimum age for voting in State Legislative Assembly elections is set at 18 years. • This provision ensures universal adult franchise. • By the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, the voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years.

subject: Polity
question: Which Article assigns the responsibility of calling for elections in a state to the Election Commission?
explanation: The responsibility for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in India, including those for State Legislatures, is assigned to the Election Commission of India under Article 324 of the Constitution.

subject: Polity
question: Controlled by state governments only. Which of the above statements is/ are true?
explanation: All India Services, such as the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and Indian Forest Service (IFoS), are specially meant for both the Union (Centre) and the States. The members of these services can work in posts under both the Central Government and the State Governments. Their provision is given under Article 312 of the Constitution • The recruitment and training of the members of these services are carried out by the Central Government (through UPSC). The final control and the authority for disciplinary action over them lie only with the Central Government. Therefore, it is incorrect to say that they are controlled only by the State Governments.

subject: Polity
question: Who is appointed as the 26th ‘Chief Election Commissioner of India’?
explanation: Gyanesh Kumar has been appointed as the 26th Chief Election Commissioner of India. He is a 1988 batch IAS officer (Kerala cadre) and has previously served as an Election Commissioner. question: Statutory grants to states by the Union government, under Article 275 of the Constitution, are primarily recommended by which body?
explanation: Under Article 275 of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the power to provide grants-in-aid to those states which are in need of financial assistance. subject: Polity
question: The Finance Commission is established under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280. Its function is to make recommendations on the distribution of taxes between the Centre and the States and on grants-in- aid to the States. • Article 268: This pertains to taxes levied by the Union but collected and retained by the States. • Article 246: This deals with the division of legislative powers between the Centre and the States; it includes the Union, State, and Concurrent Lists of the Seventh Schedule.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission of India is correct?

question: Consider the following statements: Statement I: Land and agriculture fall under the State List. Statement II: Marriage laws and adoption fall under the Concurrent List. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

explanation: According to the Indian Constitution, land and agriculture are mainly subjects of the State List. question: The term ‘Government of India’ is a legal entity under Article 300. Which of the above is/are correct?

question: Read the statements given below: Statement 1: The Constitution of India divides the legislative subjects into 3 lists, namely the Centre, State and Concurrent List. It was launched in June 2020 to provide affordable loans to street vendors. • In 2025, the scheme was updated with UPI-linked credit cards to help micro-entrepreneurs facilitate digital payments and build a formal credit score.

question: In September 2024, the Supreme Court has affirmed that the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,______applies to all women in India regardless of their religion or social background.
explanation: In September 2024, the Supreme Court clarified that the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is a secular law, which applies equally to all women in India. The Court emphasized that this Act provides protection and relief to any woman regardless of her religion or social background.

question: As per Article 279A of the Indian Constitution, the GST Council’s decisions require what kind of majority of the weighted votes of the members present and voting?
explanation: • Decisions in the GST Council, formed under Article 279A, are taken by a three-fourths majority. • The weightage of the Centre’s vote is 1/3 and the combined weightage of all the States’ votes is 2/3. • The Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson, and this system promotes cooperative federalism.

question: Which of the following accurately describes the statutory responsibilities of the Lokpal under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
options: The Lokpal is mandated to provide the President with an annual report, which will be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
The Lokpal operates under the direct administrative control of the Prime Minister’s Office.
The Lokpal must submit regular reports to the Election Commission for public disclosure.
The Lokpal is a constitutional body tasked with making final judgments in corruption cases
explanation: • The Lokpal submits its annual report to the President, which is then placed before both Houses of Parliament. • It is not under the control of the PMO; it is an independent, statutory body. The Prime Minister also comes under its jurisdiction, but for an inquiry against him special safeguards and majority approval are required.

question: Which committee recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in the Indian constitution?
explanation: • The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, constituted in 1957, suggested Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level for democratic decentralisation. • Based on this recommendation, the Panchayati Raj was inaugurated for the first time in Nagaur, Rajasthan on 2 October, 1959.
